contexts.text: The pale horse... = the damnation thence.
The pale horse = the understanding of the Word null from evils of life and the derivative falsities in the fourth or last state of the Church. AE 381.
The extinction (of the love) is... seen in the pallor of the face.

Behold a pale horse () = the understanding of the Word destroyed as to both good and truth... By pale is signified what has no vitality. In the Word, those are said to have no vitality, who are not in goods of life from truths of doctrine. (Explained.)
With those now seen there were no Knowledges of good and truth from the Word, nor any understanding of them; and, in the Spiritual World, such appear pale, like those who are devoid of life.
If the love of the world makes the head, the man appears from Heaven with a pale face, like that of a dead man, with a yellow circle round his head.
In the third Hell they appeared... pale, like the dead. He asked them whether they were dead. They said that they appear to themselves to be alive; but are such in the eyes of others.

The reason pale = evil of life and the derivative falsity - thus a pale horse, the understanding of the Word null from evils of life and the derivative falsities - is that pallor indicates and thence signifies the absence or deprivation of life; here, the absence and deprivation of spiritual life, which exists when in place of the good of life there is evil of life, and in place of the truth of faith there is falsity of faith; for then there is no spiritual life. By spiritual life is meant the life of Heaven... That by the pale horse is signified spiritual death, is evident from the words which follow...

The like is signified by pallor, or by pallid, in , (where) all faces are turned into paleness = that hence there is no good and truth, but evil and falsity; thus no spiritual life, but spiritual death. This is signified by the paleness of the face. AE 721:22.
By his faces not waxing pale () is meant that they shall not be in evils and falsities; but in goods and truths.

The reason paleness = the absence and deprivation of spiritual life, which exists when there is no good and truth, but evil and falsity, is that when man is deprived of vital heat, he grows pale, and becomes an image of death; as is the case in extreme terrors, and also when he dies; but when he dies spiritually, his face becomes either red like a coal fire, or pale like that of a corpse. Such do the infernals appear in the light of Heaven.
Paleness = the affections which are of the love of good extinguished.
I have seen three kinds of (infernals): the fiery, the black, and the pale...

He first appeared with a bright living face; then with a pale dead one; and finally with a black infernal one... Such are the successive states of the minds of those who are merely natural... The mediates of their minds, because they have falsified truths, are represented under the pallor of death...
